name: India

facts.religion: Hindu about 80%, Muslim about 14%, Christian, Sikh, Buddhist and Jain minorities

snapshot: Modi's BJP finally captured West Bengal in 2026, while a film star's new party broke Tamil Nadu's 50-year duopoly, redrawing India's federal map.
culture: India has 22 official languages and hundreds of others. Bollywood and the southern film industries in Tamil, Telugu and Malayalam reach billions, and cricket is close to a religion. Festivals like Diwali, Holi and Eid fill the calendar. Classical music and dance, yoga and a cuisine that changes every few hundred kilometres are global exports.
society: India overtook China as the most populous country in 2023 and is the fastest-growing large economy, with a booming services and tech sector. Yet hundreds of millions still farm small plots, and female workforce participation is low. Caste still shapes marriage, politics and opportunity. Critics warn of pressure on Muslims, the press and the courts under the BJP.
situation: West Bengal, India's fourth most populous state with more than 100 million people, gave the world Rabindranath Tagore and Satyajit Ray, and for half a century it was ruled first by Communists and then, since 2011, by the fiery regional leader Mamata Banerjee. It was the great prize that Narendra Modi's Hindu nationalist BJP had never won. In May 2026, it won it.

In state elections held in April, the BJP took 207 of 294 seats in West Bengal, ending Banerjee's 15-year rule and giving Modi's party control of almost all of northern, western and now eastern India (Tabla). "The 2026 West Bengal Assembly Elections will be remembered forever," Modi wrote. Analysts pointed to a consolidation of Hindu votes and a controversial revision of the voter rolls by the Election Commission (Carnegie Endowment). In Tamil Nadu, the other big upset came from cinema: Joseph Vijay, 51, one of India's biggest film stars, led his two-year-old party TVK to 108 of 234 seats, breaking a 50-year duopoly of two Dravidian parties, while sitting Chief Minister M.K. Stalin lost his own seat (ISAS). With the Left also losing Kerala, no Indian state is now governed by the Communist parties that once ran three of them. Critics warn the results show power concentrating in Delhi at the expense of the federal system that holds a country of 1.4 billion and 22 official languages together.
power: A federal parliamentary republic. The prime minister leads the majority in the 543-seat Lok Sabha; the 28 states have their own elected assemblies and chief ministers who control policing, health and much more. The president is largely ceremonial.
holders: Prime Minister Narendra Modi (BJP), in office since 2014.

conflicts.name: India-Pakistan confrontation (Kashmir and the post-May 2025 standoff)
